n01a.text: Every record on Propchain is attested.

n01b.text: But attestation proves provenance, not truth. A rent roll full of phantom tenants can be perfectly signed, and perfectly false.

n02.text: And consensus can't decide whether a tenant exists.

n03.text: Most fraud loss is misstated income, or diverted closing funds. Both have a truth the platform can see: cash.

n05.text: The defence is six layers, each stopping what the one below cannot: identity, provenance, corroboration, bonds, professional signatures, and memory.

n06.text: What gets through all six is what insurance prices.

n07.text: Corroboration first. One asset's annual rent, from four sources.

n08.text: The rent roll says one million and twenty thousand euros. The manager's ledger agrees, but it follows the seller: one source, not two.

n09.text: Bank receipts show nine hundred and fifty-eight thousand. Tenants confirm nine fifty-five.

n10.text: Cash outranks documents. The quorum settles at nine fifty-six, and the field reaches level A three: reconciled to cash.

n11.text: Counterparties can require a level, field by field, from A zero to A five. And A four needs something new: capital at risk.

n12.text: A bond is a holdback with rules instead of lawyers. An illustrative deal: thirteen million euros, eight hundred thousand of attested income, a six point one five percent cap rate.

n13.text: The seller warrants that income within five percent, for twelve months. A forty-thousand tolerance.

n14.text: The bond covers the buyer's loss at a ten percent miss: eighty thousand over the cap rate. One point three million, held in a yield-bearing escrow.

n15.text: Twelve months of bank receipts decide.

n16.text: Income of seven sixty is a five percent miss, inside tolerance. The bond is released in full.

n17.text: At seven twenty, the miss is five points beyond tolerance. Half the bond goes to the buyer. Pro rata, never all or nothing.

n18a.text: That only works where a later truth exists, that a contract can read.

n18b.text: Rent against receipts. Title against the registry. Bondable.

n18c.text: Building condition? Only with a referee, named in advance.

n20.text: So who posts the capital? Usually, it isn't new money. The bond replaces the holdback, or W and I premium, a sale already carries.

n21.text: The seller can self-bond. A surety can post for a fee. Or the buyer can hold a policy, on the same trigger.

n22.text: The market is the middle one: sureties quoting on the same attested record, with fees that fall with level and track record.

n23.text: Sellers bond only if certainty, a higher rank, firm debt, speed, is worth more than the cost. That has to be measured, not assumed.

n24b.text: As for a native insurer: a data partner needs no capital. An M G A underwrites on a carrier's capital. An own carrier needs a licence, and solvency capital. The realistic route is A, then B.

n25.text: The edge is observation. The platform sees what was claimed at close, and what was realised for years after. That pairing is a loss curve no incumbent has.

n26.text: So short-tail, parametric cover comes first, because it teaches fastest. Float comes last.

n27a.text: It's a working draft, and the numbers are illustrative. But the plan is simple.

n27b.text: Measure first. Bond what is measured. Insure the rest.
